Chelo Taste of Persia is a good Persian restaurant on a busy street with dine in, delivery and takeout options.

I came here based on the online reviews and pictures for takeout. I ordered a grilled chicken plate with rice which came with garlic sauce, pita bread, hummus and lentil soup.

The employee who offered me some friendly advice about the menu and took my order gave me some helpful recommendations and a generous amount of food for my takeout order.

While I was waiting for my order, I noticed an unhoused person walking around the restaurant, probably taking momentary shelter from the extreme heat outside that day. Different employees and restaurant owners will respond differently to these types of situations in my experience.

The employee asked the person if they needed help or assistance and stood behind my chair, seemingly offering me a little safety for my heavy purse. Then the employee proceeded to load up a large cup with ice and gave it to to the non paying customer as a gift, which in consideration of how hot it was outside, I think was a pretty special gift.

Some of us know how valuable a cup of ice can be on a hot day, I used to buy a cup of ice when I couldn't afford to buy a beverage as a child and it was sometimes pretty important for my health.

Everything I ordered was very good and it all stayed warm for a good amount of time so that I ended up eating two warm meals that afternoon.

The rice had a nice texture and flavor, like a pilaf. The thick yellow lentil soup was my favorite part of the meal, five stars. The grilled white meat chicken was lean, and lightly seasoned, which I prefer to highly marinated myself.

The interior of the restaurant is cute and very clean. The service is excellent. Good people= Five stars!

This spot caught our eye. We stopped in with quite an appetite. This place looks like a takeout spot, but they have a nice small dining room. You order at the counter and they call you when ready

We started with some Pita and the Garlic Shallot Yogurt dip. It was good. Note, the Persian Iced tea is good but very sweetened.

I ordered the Shish Kabob and the Chicken Kabob. Both were tender and delicious. The saffron rice served made a perfect complement.

My wife had the Chicken Koobedeh and the Shish Kabob. Both plates came with a small lentil soup.  They also give you a choice of small dips, such as hummus, to go with the pita bread.

The best item was the chicken kabob. It was very moist and flavorful. All the other skewers were good but not as good as the chicken.

The portions were generous; we took half of each plate home! Definitely filled out appetite. Lastly, I couldn't resist the homemade bakklava.

Next time I'm back in Van Nuys, I'll have to stop by again.

I tried Carnival recently and overall had a decent experience. I ordered the shawarma and lamb kebab combination. The shawarma was tasty and flavorful, though a bit on the greasy side. The lentil soup was also delicious and comforting. I appreciated that they bring out free warm pita bread, which is a nice touch. However, because it’s very thin, it gets hard after just a few minutes. I think one thicker, regular pita would be better than three very thin ones.

As for the lamb kebab, I wasn’t as impressed. It came out pink and closer to medium-rare, which I personally didn’t enjoy. To the waiter’s credit, he offered to replace it, but I didn’t have time to wait for another one. For dessert, I tried the knafeh. It was different than others I’ve had but still light and delicious. The waiter mentioned it was the freshest one, which was nice, though it made me wonder about the rest.

Overall, the food was decent and the service was friendly. Nothing to rave about, but it was a solid experience if you’re in the area.

2x Double Cheeseburger / 5⭐!

Bill's Hamburgers in Van Nuys has been open since 1965 on a quiet, industrial-leaning part of Oxnard where they serve American classics, hamburgers, cheeseburgers, hot dogs, sandwiches, breakfast items and chili. It's a cash-only business so make sure you bring some cash with you.

Bill's is one of those kinds of local spots where the 'ones in the know' will rave about and for good reason. They have a decent sized menu but I had heard many times over the years that their burgers are the way to go. While I was waiting for my order, I heard regulars ordering other items so it is safe to assume there is more to love than their hamburgers. I'd like to go back and try their breakfast sandwiches.

The burgers I had were delicious. There is an art in perfecting a menu and Bill's has achieved just such a perfection with his sixty years in business! The burgers were very well cooked, well seasoned, had nice crispy edges, and were extremely tasty.

The prices are still quite affordable. The service was quick and efficient for my visit. I would recommend you find street parking. The burger shack has a large parking lot next door but there are multiple signs warning Bill's guests from using the parking.

I also loved how cozy and personal the setting felt. While they don't have seating, they do have some bar counters outside. I took my burgers to my car. I loved the ramshackle shack look of their restaurant and the no-frills, effortlessly tasty food on their menu.

I recognize that Bill is set to retire or maybe he already has. But his legacy and his classic American menu will live on as long as there are people who care about quality food at good prices. They are worth the visit!

text.text:
The words classic, vintage, old school and no frills come to mind when describing Bills Burgers!

Probably one of the most consistent burger stands in California. Having grace this small stand for a decade, I can say this is one of my favorite burger joints.

This family business starts with Bill, who is currently retired but is seen around the stand premise. I recently had a pleasant conversation with this legend. Bill told me his back story and how he has been grilling burgers at this location for 35 years. Can you imagine all that seasoning on that grill throughout the decades. Bill is now 97 and I was honored to listen to him while I waited for my order. His wife (sorry I don’t know her name) and her son Douglas have taken reigns and they haven’t missed a beat. The legacy continues!

Cash only, no phone call orders, there is a breakfast and lunch rush. No fries , only chips and cans of soda. May sell out before 3. No place to sit.

I absolutely love this place. My go to is the triple cheese with bacon and a side of lay chips. The patties are thin and seasoned well, with gooey American cheese, a nice soft bun with veggies and homemade sauce. The bacon is legit. You will get burger juice all over yourself as you bite into this heavenly sandwich.

I will keep coming here til they close. Thankful for Bill and his family. Great business to support.

I first came to this place 6 years ago and remember it fondly. My options and time for food where limited at the time, and having this place felt so abundant and delicious. Honestly, it's still the same place. The food is pretty dang good, especially if you go for your favorites once you find them, and they're not trying to be gourmet or transcendent.. it's an AYCE buffet. You pay your chunk of money, around 28 bucks, and you eat as much as you want... Simple... I gravitate towards their sushi, chicken wings, fried shrimp, and surprisingly good barbecue ribs.. the pork buns have always been on par with a good quality home steamed version too. Some of the stuffed clams and creations often end up being favorites too, but that changes every visit. If you want buffet desserts following your savory meal, this is not the one, there's a few mid to bad cake squares and such. The quality and cleanliness is good, and Ive never felt off or uncomfortable even after eating too much.

The dining area and buffet is roomy and fairly crowded on a Saturday around 2:00p. Especially with lots of large families.

I think this place is worth your time and money if you are really hungry and craving some simple, good food from the cuisines they offer. I give it 5 stars because they're doing exactly what they're trying to do.. offer a big selection of decent foods and as much as you want of it.

For the win USED to be a definite top 3 smashburger spot!
(When there were only a few of them)
How times have changed.....
Yesterday I went to the Van Nuys location, & took my (9&11 year old) nephews.
It had to be 100° inside there. ? & no water.
I ordered: 2 single cheeseburgers, 1 double cheeseburger, 2 small fries, & 2 shakes. Over $60!
I got our food, & asked for ketchup. He said, "we don't carry ketchup anymore".
So you sell french fries, but don't have ketchup? "Nope"
Then, my double cheeseburger didn't have pickles on it.
I told him, & he said there was.
I lifted the bun & showed him.
He then told me they were between the patties. So I completely pulled my double smashburger apart, just for him to say, "hum".
He then gave me 10 pickels in a pice of aluminum foil, & said, "sorry about that".
UNBELIEVABLE!
From one of my all time favorite smashburger spots, that I have steered 100s of customers to, to a place I will now tell people not to visit!
I would have had a better experience at a Carl's Jr or McDonald's.
With so many good smashburger joints out there,
( Burgers Never Say Die/Burgers She Wrote/Goldburger/Heavy Handed/Let's Smash/Burger 3000/Easy Street Burgers....)
the lack of your quality is going to start losing you business.
Now, with all the locations, you don't seem to have the same product.
Wish you would have stayed small.
